newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Formosa Plastics in US$800 mln US plant.
newsitem.headline: Formosa Plastics in US$800 mln US plant.

text.p: Taiwan's Formosa Plastics Corp said on Wednesday it has applied to the U.S. government for a US$800 million expansion to build a petrochemical complex in Texas.

"Our U.S. subsidiary Formosa Plastics USA has applied to the U.S. Environmental Protection Administration for the US$800 million expansion in our Texas plant," Formosa vice-president Lee Chih-tsun told Reuters by telephone.

The petrochemical complex will mainly include an ethylene plant, which has an annual production capacity of 880,000 tonnes, and a polypropylene plant, which has an annual capacity of 300,000 tonnes, he said.
"The expansion will mainly supply our group's own usage," Lee said.
Formosa expects to gain approval for the expansion by the end of 1996, and construction will take two years, Lee said.
Formosa's existing Texas plant has an annual production capacity of 680,000 tonnes of ethylene, he said.

Formosa group launched its US$9 billion sixth naphtha cracker project in 1993 in central Taiwan. Construction of the complex, including a naphtha cracker and oil refinery, will take six years to complete.
The complex's main products will include ethylene, designed with an annual capacity of 1.35 million tonnes.
After completion of all its planned expansion in Taiwan and the United States, the group's combined annual ethylene production will reach 2.91 million tonnes.
The group, Taiwan's largest industrial conglomerate, has three key members: Formosa Plastics, Nan Ya Plastics and Formosa Chemical and Fibre.
